knowledge_point.title: Calculating a Unit Vector Parallel to a Given Vector

question.:question/problem: Let $b=\begin{bmatrix}-12 \\ -5\end{bmatrix}$. Find a unit vector that is parallel to $b$ and points the same direction.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u &= \frac{b}{|b|}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|b| &= \sqrt{(-12)^2+(-5)^2} \\
&= \sqrt{144+25} \\
&= \sqrt{169} \\
&= 13\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $b$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u &= \frac{b}{|b|} \\
&= \frac{1}{13}\cdot (b) \\
&= \frac{1}{13}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}-12 \\ -5\end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix}- \frac{12}{13} \\ - \frac{5}{13}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

&= \begin{bmatrix}- \frac{12}{13} \\ - \frac{5}{13}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Calculating a Unit Vector Parallel to a Given Vector

question.:question/problem: Let $a=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}$ and $b=\begin{bmatrix}9 \\ 38\end{bmatrix}$. Find a unit vector that is parallel to $2a+b$ and points the same direction.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector and points the same direction, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u &= \frac{2a+b}{|2a+b|}\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's compute the sum:

$$
\begin{aligned}2a+b &= 2\cdot \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}9 \\ 38\end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}9 \\ 38\end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix}0+(9) \\ 2+(38)\end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix}9 \\ 40\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|2a+b| &= \sqrt{(9)^2+(40)^2} \\
&= \sqrt{1681} \\
&= 41\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $2a+b$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u &= \frac{2a+b}{|2a+b|} \\
&= \frac{1}{41}\cdot (2a+b) \\
&= \frac{1}{41}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}9 \\ 40\end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix}\frac{9}{41} \\ \frac{40}{41}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$
